requirements.evidence: Full contract is present: enums (app/Enums/TicketStatus.php:7-8, TicketChannel.php:7-9), InactiveQueueException extends RuntimeException (app/Exceptions/InactiveQueueException.php:7), Queue model with fillable/casts/relations (app/Models/Queue.php:10-37), Entity::queues() (app/Models/Entity.php:46-49), migrations with cascades, unique (queue_id, code) and the recommended index (create_tickets_table.php:16,26-27). IssueTicket rejects negative priority (IssueTicket.php:21-23), re-reads and locks the queue in the transaction ("Queue::whereKey(...)->lockForUpdate()->firstOrFail()", line 33) and retries on unique violations (lines 50-56). nextCode orders by id, skips malformed codes and pads to 3 digits (Ticket.php:75-91). The write-once updating hook is at Ticket.php:46-55, and the factory has a null code filled by the creating hook plus forQueue (TicketFactory.php:31,41-44). Gap: Ticket::call (Ticket.php:101-120) checks status on the possibly stale in-memory instance with no lock or conditional update, so a second, stale or concurrent call can overwrite called_at/called_by_user_id, which breaks 'called exactly once'.

conventions.evidence: Ships no tests at all, which violates the core 'No production code without a test; everything implemented ships with a test' convention. CHANGELOG.md is not updated under [Unreleased]. Authorization in Ticket::call is a hand-rolled EntityMembership query (Ticket.php:105-111) rather than a policy/gate. On the positive side, the domain write goes through app/Actions/IssueTicket, $fillable is set deliberately, migrations have down() methods, and business-rules.md and database-schema.md are updated.

security.evidence: Membership is checked before calling (Ticket.php:105-111, throws AuthorizationException). Fillable is explicit. Queue state is read under a row lock. There is no HTTP/Livewire surface. Limited gap: call() does not re-check status under a lock, so concurrent members can both 'call' the same ticket and the last writer overwrites called_by_user_id. The write-once hook also allows status to be set back to waiting via update.

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files (no tests/ paths). None of the specified behaviours are covered: code sequencing edge cases (A999->A1000, deletion gaps, A-X skipping), inactive/stale queue rejection, negative priority, write-once LogicException, single call, or non-member AuthorizationException.

simplicity.evidence: The implementation is mostly direct and reuses Eloquent features (creating/updating hooks, factory for()). Small redundancies: IssueTicket passes 'code' => Ticket::nextCode(...) (line 41) although the creating hook already allocates it; the 'catch (InactiveQueueException $e) { throw $e; }' block (lines 48-49) is a no-op; isUniqueViolation repeats the same check twice ('$e->getCode() === '23000' || (string) $e->getCode() === '23000''). nextCode plucks every code in the queue on each issuance (Ticket.php:77).

readability.evidence: Names are clear and methods are small. PHPDoc covers nextCode and call (Ticket.php:69-74, 94-100). Comments explain the locking and write-once intent. Minor noise comes from the redundant catch/rethrow and the duplicated getCode comparison.

scope.evidence: Every file serves the task: models, enums, exception, action, factories, two migrations, Entity::queues() and the two docs the task asked to update. There are no unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The change adds a whole domain core with no Pest/PHPUnit tests, against the project's mandatory test-first convention, and none of the many specified edge cases are verified.

call() checks status on the in-memory model without locking or a conditional update, so a stale instance or a concurrent call can call an already-called ticket again and overwrite called_at/called_by_user_id.
Membership authorization is a hand-rolled EntityMembership query instead of going through a policy/gate as the conventions require.
The conventions require a CHANGELOG entry under [Unreleased]; it is not updated.
The write-once guard permits any status change, including reverting a called ticket to waiting via save().
isUniqueViolation treats any SQLSTATE 23000 (also FK/not-null violations on MySQL/SQLite) as a code collision, so it retries errors that are not collisions.
nextCode loads every code of the queue on each issuance; its cost grows with queue history.
The InactiveQueueException catch-and-rethrow is a no-op, and the getCode comparison is duplicated.
The code is computed explicitly although the Ticket creating hook already allocates it when it is empty.

review.summary: The change implements queues, tickets, enums, factories, the IssueTicket action and the doc updates faithfully to the contract, including stale-queue locking, code sequencing rules and write-once enforcement. It ships no tests at all, which violates the project's mandatory test-first convention, and Ticket::call can be applied twice on a stale or concurrent instance. It needs substantial work (a full test suite plus a fix for the call race) before approval.
